Ron Smith & David Berg COMPASS “The real estate market is currently in a standoff,” says Berg. “Buyers want a price that hedges against the economy. Sellers think their house is the exception to the economy. Everybody’s waiting for the other person to blink.” This stalemate hasn’t stopped the duo from having another successful year, with a sales volume of $645 million to prove it. “Social media has made it very easy to look like a top producer without being one,” Smith says. “Sellers figured that out, and now the first question we get in a listing appointment isn’t about marketing, it’s, ‘How many homes did you actually sell last year?’ That’s a healthy change.” Mauricio Umansky Courtesy of Subject The Umansky Team THE AGENCY Mauricio Umansky has built his team around his family, including his daughters, Farrah and Alexia, and dad, Eduardo. Since Umansky founded The Agency in 2011, it has grown into a global brand, but Umansky’s heart remains in L.A. “The weather here in Los Angeles allows for year-round indoor/outdoor living, which makes for very innovative architecture,” he says. $13.3M The Meadow House, at 2 Rumsen Trace in Carmel, listed by the Umansky Team at The Agency. Manny Espinoza Shauna Walters & Nicole Plaxen Courtesy of Subject (2) Shauna Walters & Nicole Plaxen SOTHEBY’S INTERNATIONAL REALTY With $1 billion in career sales, the duo has among the most impressive celebrity clientele in the business. Brayden & Rayni Williams Courtesy of Subject (2) Brayden & Rayni Williams THE BEVERLY HILLS ESTATES Although the two are no longer romantically involved, the colorful duo’s professional life keeps swinging, with $1.6 billion in sales in 2025. title: Jon Cohen Named President Of Lipovsky & Stein’s Wonderlab Banner
full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Jon Cohen Named President Of Lipovsky & Stein’s Wonderlab Banner Comedian Mojo Brookzz Bringing Debut Special ‘I Know You Lying’ To Netflix In October ‘The Family Stone’ Sequel Set At Searchlight With Claire Danes, Rachel McAdams, Sarah Jessica Parker & Many More Returning View All September 14, 2026 7:00am John Cohen, Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein Courtesy/Getty Jon Cohen has joined Wonderlab , the newly launched production company of Final Destination: Bloodlines helmers Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein , as President. Cohen comes over from J.J. Abrams’ Bad Robot, where he most recently served as Head of Film. “We are so incredibly excited to launch Wonderlab with Jon,” Lipovsky and Stein said. “During his time at Bad Robot, Jon had a discerning eye for discovering some of the brightest genre filmmakers and writers and empowering them to make smart, original movies that connect with audiences. From our first conversations, Jon blew us away with his intelligence and deep creative insights about how to craft great stories. He shares our love of making unique and elevated films that are also incredibly fun and entertaining, and his collaborative nature is a perfect fit for the iterative way we plan to develop new movies at Wonderlab.” Related Stories News Zach Lipovsky And Adam B. Stein Ink First-Look Deal At Sony, Set 'Metal Gear Solid' Movie News 'Final Destination Bloodlines' Duo Zach Lipovsky & Adam B. Stein To Direct Animated 'Venom' Movie For Sony During his tenure at Bad Robot, Cohen produced a wide-ranging slate of features, including 10 Cloverfield Lane as co-producer, The Cloverfield Paradox and Overlord as executive producer. He was also a producer on Lou for Netflix, The End of Oak Street for Warner Bros., and the upcoming J.T. Mollner/Brie Larson film Skeletons , which Sony is set to release in 2027. Watch on Deadline Originally from Highland Park, Illinois, Cohen held executive positions at The Donners Company and Davis Entertainment before joining Bad Robot. “I couldn’t be more thrilled to be joining forces with Zach and Adam, and to be on the ground floor of what they’re creating with Wonderlab,” said Cohen. “I’ve admired the guys’ filmmaking for a while, and their FINAL DESTINATION: BLOODLINES was the sort of clever, impeccably made and wildly entertaining genre movie that so many aspire to create but very few can. As I’ve gotten to know them better, I’ve only grown more impressed with their ambition, work ethic, taste, story sense and talent, and how it’s all fused to an incredibly collaborative process and mindset that makes everyone who works with them long to work with them again. Cohen continued, “I’m very grateful to them for this opportunity, and to Sony Pictures for the faith they’ve placed in Wonderlab, and I look forward to making thrilling, surprising and emotionally resonant genre movies with this group for years to come.” Under a first-look deal with Sony Pictures that has the company developing projects across all of their film labels, Wonderlab projects announced so far include an animated Venom movie for Sony Pictures Animation; video game adaptation Metal Gear Solid ; and The Earthling , based on the Jonathan Marty short story, with the latter two projects being developed for Columbia Pictures. Founders Lipovsky and Stein broke out as the directors of New Line’s Final Destination: Bloodlines , which is now the highest-grossing film in its franchise at around $317 million worldwide. The films above are just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to their slate, which also includes a sequel to their 2018 sci-fi thriller Freaks , Warner Bros./Amblin’s Gremlins 3 , Universal/Amblin’s Long Lost , Paramount’s The Traveler , and more. “Wonderlab’s mission is to make movies using an iterative process that surrounds our creators with candid feedback from test audiences and other filmmakers,” Stein and Lipovsky stated. “It’s a process we’ve built over many years to make sure a film is the best it can be. We’re grateful to Tom, Sanford, and Peter at Sony for helping us scale this process across a slate of awesome films in the pipeline.” ‘Prima Facie’, ‘Wilson Shedd’, ‘Evil Genius’ Reviewed; Deadline Studio Vids Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Producer Remembered By Industry ‘Adolescence’ Scribe Says Writers Using AI To “Cheat” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Brews Up $46M WW & $30M In U.S. Read More About: 1 Comments

title: Six Years After Starring Father Died Soon After TIFF Short Premiere, ‘Strong Son’ Director Returns With Grief Drama
full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All September 14, 2026 6:45am Mandeep-Sodhi, Amrit-Parbhakar in Strong Son Markus Henkel Director Ian Bawa’s debut feature, Strong Son, explores the irony of a South Asian bodybuilder bulking up at a local gym just as his mental health goes downhill, and all while he cares at home for his strong-willed elderly father who is seeing his own physical health markedly weaken. And much as the movie’s main character, Harvey Singh, played by Mandeep Sodhi, becomes emotionally broken due to his father’s outdated idea about how a real man must act – hide your emotions, don’t appear powerless and get married – Bawa himself has pushed the limits of his own storytelling vulnerability as a director to capture his real-life grief over the loss of both his parents. Related Stories Movies 'Seventeen' Director Justin Ducharme Talks Portraying Struggling Sex Workers as BFFs in Gritty Vancouver Movies Zack Snyder's 'The Last Photograph': First Reactions “The feature itself is as truthful as a narrative and a personal narrative, without being a documentary,” Bawa tells The Hollywood Reporter ahead of a world premiere for Strong Son at the Toronto Film Festival. His feature, in fact, expands on a 2020 short film, also called Strong Son , that featured Bawa’s real-life father, Jagdeep Singh Bawa, as a South Asian father giving advice to his son as he trains at a local gym, with the mantra, “My son is very strong.” That 3-minute film, shot on Super 8, world premiered at TIFF during a pandemic-era festival online, and with Bawa, buoyed by his festival success and his father at his side, already having a feature adaptation in mind. But only three weeks later, after the first look in Toronto, Bawa’s father died from a sudden heart attack. And that shock death followed his mother, Pritam Bawa, passing away in 2007 after a battle with breast cancer and 36 years of marriage. “All of a sudden, my life blew up in the other way, where it was embarrassing, this movie, because it felt like people were pitying me and in my head I was dealing with grief rather than working on the feature,” Bawa recalled. The Winnipeg-based filmmakers explored his grief in another 2024 short film, My Son Went Quiet and other short films. But his first feature, Strong Son , captures the strained relationship between Harvey and his father after moving back into the family home, only to battle severe panic attacks and crying fits as he feels the strain of being a parental caregiver. And Harvey faces his overbearing father’s disappointment most glaringly with the public humiliation of an emotional breakdown while taking part in an amateur wrestling match the bodybuilder entered to prove his physical strength. Bawa says most every scene in Strong Son , and much of the dialogue, was taken directly from his personal experience caring for his father over the 10 years before his death, as the feature thematically explores toxic masculinity in South Asian culture. “Those words were spoken to me, as my Dad told me to stop crying, you’re acting like a woman, you’re acting like your mother. It’s one of the weird trauma moments that sit with you,” he explains. Another source material is the original emergency phone call Bawa in real life made to paramedics on discovering his father in heart arrest, which is recreated in Strong Son the feature. “It’s all real, from the true 911 call. I have this stuff, what else am I going to do with it? And it’s his legacy at this point – no one’s going to remember my Dad, except me,” he explains. At the same time, the sparse filmmaking style behind Strong Son — which combines stationary shots in quiet moments between Harvey and his father at home, with action-driven scenes set in the local gym – springs in part from the lead Sodhi being a bodybuilder-turned-actor since leaving India for Canada in 2011. And Amrit Parbhakar as Jagdeep Singh only came on board for his first film lead role just one week before Bawa started production on the low-budget indie, and after an earlier actor set to play Harvey’s father dropped out. Another hurdle was Parbhakar having gone blind two years before Strong Son was shot, which called for improvisation between director and lead actor on set during rehearsals and faking an eye line when the camera, handled by cinematographer and producer Markus Henkel, rolled. “We shot backwards. We’d start with close-ups of everyone, then do his (Parbhakar) last,” as a third assistant helped him learn lines phonetically as in effect his personal assistant. Another irony about Bawa as a filmmaker as his personal story is now ready for the world to see coming out of TIFF is he claims to be useless at talking about his inner feelings and emotions to his therapist. “I’m an extrovert. I do like to talk, but I’m really bad at therapy,” he insists. Bawa hopes his feature, as it explores family grief and intergenerational connection, does resonate with audiences. As for what’s next for the Canadian filmmaker after his debut feature premieres in Toronto, Bawa has a couple of scripts on the go, including a horror pic. The other is a dark comedy about a South Asian man who is balding and has wrinkles as he ages, and so decides to kidnap his illegitimate son to take him to Mexico for a skin and hair transplant. “Whatever the next one is, it has to be extremely different. Because that’s my rule in life. You have to pivot and try new things. Otherwise, what am I doing? I’m not going to learn anything,” Bawa says. THR

title: WME’s Sleek New Headquarters Give Agents Every Reason to Come to the Office (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Oren Peleg Plus Icon Oren Peleg View All September 14, 2026 6:30am The lobby of WME’s new Beverly Hills headquarters as realized by the interior design firm Gensler. Eric Laignel Photography Richard Weitz, co-chairman of the WME group, is standing in the lobby of the agency’s new Beverly Hills headquarters on a recent afternoon. The space suddenly swells with agents, assistants, clients and others shuffling through for lunch. Some people split off to sit for a meal at 1898 — the plush new lobby restaurant operated by Wolfgang Puck that has taken over for Jack & Ben’s — while others grab something light from the café and huddle inside the many wood-and-velvet booths taking up the center of the lobby, creating what is effectively the office’s new town square. Weitz watches as people come together to eat, chat and even just throw a quick “hey, nice to see you.” He believes work-from-home arrangements aren’t suited to WME’s business. Representation always has been about relationships, he says. Hollywood, in other words, is an in-person job. “Even though the industry is changing, there are two things you can’t replace: community and collaboration,” explains Weitz. So when he and Christian Muirhead became co-chairmen of the storied agency in 2022, they made it a priority to renovate the headquarters to foster more face-to-face interaction. They asked global design firm Gensler to reimagine WME’s aging offices along Camden Drive, which hadn’t had a refresh in more than two decades. “WME had been in this building for such a long time, and every time some other tenant moved out, they took over the space,” explains Brian Barry, Gensler’s design director, who led the renovation. As a result, the agency’s 10 floors were a Frankensteined amalgamation of styles flattened out by white paint and a vague Y2K futurism aesthetic: “It was all kind of cohesive, but not really.” Eric Laignel Photography Eric Laignel Photography Over four years, Barry transformed the headquarters by replacing the sterility of the white paint with layers of organic materials (rich woods, brass, leather) and designing smaller, human-centric spaces where agents and clients could meet. A large, state-of-the-art listening lounge was built on the seventh floor so musicians could play new work for their team in a comfortable, modern setting. On the ground floor, the Chaplin Theater provides a similar experience for such WME filmmaker clients as Christopher Nolan, Ryan Coogler and Maggie Gyllenhaal. “We wanted every creative environment in the building to support the work at the highest level,” says Weitz. Adds Muirhead: “We spend our days working with people who obsess over every detail of their craft. It only felt right to create spaces that meet that same standard.” Across the office floors, emphasis was placed on functionality. “The agents and their assistants have a very unique, very direct relationship,” says Barry. “So we created a sort of town hall on every floor with conference rooms and the improved pantries as a central destination.” Eric Laignel Photography The main design elements for these office spaces are the nearly 400 artworks hand-selected and supplied by Creative Arts Partners, whom WME had discovered after they supplied the artwork for Kevin Hart’s offices at HartBeat. “Our goal was, how do we put together a collection as creative as the amazing talent that WME represents?” explains Brian Ludlow, co-founder and CEO of Creative Arts Partners. The result is a beautiful array of original paintings, photography and even sculptural works that pepper the offices with names like Petra Cortright and Spencer Lewis. It’s been years of disruption and change for WME, from the pandemic to the WGA and SAG strikes and the four-year construction of the office itself. Now, Weitz says he’s excited to have everyone back in the new office. Eric Laignel Photography This story appeared in the Sept. 9 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

title: Former Tubi Production Exec Ashla Soter Joins Post House Digital Sword
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Nightsleeper’ Season 2: Colin Morgan, Madeleine Mantock & Christian Cooke Lead Return Of BBC Thriller Drama International Insider: European TV In Peril; Venice & TIFF Latest; Mercedes Ron Interview Cricket Legend Virender Sehwag To Host ‘Rise And Fall’ Season 2 For Prime Video View All September 14, 2026 7:00am Ashla Soter Digital Sword EXCLUSIVE: Post house Digital Sword has hired former Tubi production exec Ashla Soter. A month after exiting the streamer, she’s been named Executive Producer and SVP of Production at Digital Sword, where she will assume oversight of production across the company’s full slate, working with studios, brands, and agencies alongside Digital Sword’s global editorial, color, VFX, and finishing teams. Soter will also continue to produce select projects independently. At Tubi, she was the first production hire for the streamer’s originals push and spent three years there. She was in charge of original content production and oversaw more than 150 scripted and unscripted titles, including Sidelined: The QB and Me , which was a big seven-day ratings hit and grew into a three film franchise. Related Stories News Playhouse Studios Buys Halo Post Assets & Launches Playhouse Post News Adobe Previews AI-Powered Video Editing System 'Project Frame Forward' Besides being a production exec, Soter is an independent producer and over the past decade has worked on the likes of feature doc The Chainsaw Artist . Watch on Deadline “We needed someone who could run a full slate and hold the standard on every job,” said Cal Laird and Joan Pabon, founders of Digital Sword, in a statement. “Ashla has done exactly that, at the highest level.” “This team cares about making great work more than anything else, and it shows in everything they touch,” added Soter. Founded by Laird and Pabon, Digital Sword represents editors and artists and works across film, television, advertising and music.
